dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: An indexed run-package type for dimensions m and n. dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target universally quantifies over inhabitants of this highly restricted package rather than over arbitrary matrices.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: A proposition indexed by a run. Its supplied constructor D004 certifies a chain of first-column normalization, residual, norm-equality, and norm-bound statements.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines all assumptions implicit in the quantified variable run.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes LocalDef002 run a conjunction-like certificate yielding ||A[:,0]-Q[:,0]R00||₂ ≤ epsilonM ||A[:,0]||₂ through the recorded equality and inequality chain.

binders: m and n are implicit universally quantified natural numbers.
run is universally quantified over LocalDef001 m n and therefore packages all data and assumptions below.
The run contains A,Q ∈ R^(m×n), R ∈ R^(n×n), epsilonM ∈ R, a family B_s of square real matrices for s=1,...,n, and a first-column perturbation matrix G1 ∈ R^(m×m).
All matrix and vector indices are zero-based finite indices.
hypotheses: The map R^n → R^m given by x ↦ Ax is injective.
R is upper triangular: R_ij = 0 whenever j < i.
For every s=1,...,n, B_s is a chosen two-sided inverse of the leading principal block R_s = R[0:s,0:s]: B_s R_s = I_s and R_s B_s = I_s.
Writing a=A[:,0], q=Q[:,0], and r=R_00, the run contains G1 ∈ R^(m×m) such that r>0, q_i=(a_i+(G1a)_i)/r for every i, and ||G1||₂→₂ ≤ epsilonM.
conclusions: LocalDef002 run is inhabited, meaning that its full first-column certificate is available.
If E=A[:,0]-Q[:,0][r] is viewed as an m by 1 matrix and e=a-qr as a vector, then E_i0=e_i for every i.
The sole-column norm of E equals ||e||₂.
Consequently, the recorded chain yields ||A[:,0]-Q[:,0]R_00||₂ ≤ epsilonM ||A[:,0]||₂, where the left side is the Euclidean norm of the first-column residual.
mathematical_definitions: For p∈N, Fin p is identified with {0,...,p-1}.
For a square real matrix M, ||M||₂→₂ denotes the matrix norm selected by the supplied L2-operator norm instance.
For s=1,...,n, R_s is the s by s leading principal submatrix with entries (R_s)_ij=R_ij for 0≤i,j<s.
beta(m,1)=1; for s≠1, beta(m,s)=2s sqrt(2m)+2 sqrt(s).
C(m,s)=alpha(m,s)+2 beta(m,s). Thus C(m,1)=m+4, while for s>1, C(m,s)=(7/2)ms²-(3/2)ms+16s+4s sqrt(2m)+4 sqrt(s).
a=A[:,0], q=Q[:,0], r=R_00, e=a-qr, and E is the m by 1 matrix with E_i0=e_i.

translation.proposition_plain_english: For every pair of natural dimensions and every packaged run satisfying the stated positivity, dimension, injectivity, triangularity, leading-block invertibility, smallness, and first-column normalization conditions, the run has a first-column residual certificate. Using the same perturbation matrix G1 stored in the run, the residual A[:,0]-Q[:,0]R_00 equals -G1A[:,0]; its Euclidean norm equals ||G1A[:,0]||₂ and is bounded first by ||G1||₂→₂||A[:,0]||₂ and then by epsilonM||A[:,0]||₂.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition is conditional on an inhabitant run. It does not assert that such a run exists, so it is vacuous for dimensions or data admitting no run; in particular no run can exist when m=0, n=0, or n>m.
The leading-block inverses B_s and G1 are supplied components of run, not witnesses whose existence is independently proved by the target.
Only the first, zero-indexed column is covered. No residual or error bound is asserted for columns 1 through n-1.
No statement says that Q is orthogonal or has normalized columns.
No global equation A=QR or approximate factorization statement is encoded.

R is only required to be upper triangular, with R_00>0. No positivity or nonzero condition is imposed directly on later diagonal entries, although the supplied two-sided inverses force every leading block to be invertible.
The injectivity of A, upper triangularity of R, leading-block inverses, and smallness inequalities restrict the run domain but do not occur in the fields of the first-column certificate D004.
epsilonM is an arbitrary nonnegative real satisfying the packaged assumptions; the proposition does not identify it with machine unit roundoff or any particular floating-point format.
All quantities and equalities are over exact real numbers. No floating-point operations, rounding map, execution trace, probability, or computed approximation is encoded.
The conclusion predicate is a proof package containing intermediate equalities and inequalities, not merely the final residual inequality.

The relative bound remains meaningful when a=0 because the stored normalization equation and norm chain then force the certified residual norm to be zero; no separate nonzero assumption on ||a||₂ is present.
No uniqueness is claimed for G1 or for the chosen leading-block inverses.
ambiguities: The body of the matrix L2-operator norm instance delegates its norm field to an auxiliary construction not included in the packet. The translation therefore denotes exactly the supplied matrix norm symbolically as ||·||₂→₂; its lower-level normalization cannot be reconstructed solely from the dossier.

The constructors or fields of Nat.AtLeastTwo and NeZero are not supplied. Their concrete instances are used only for numeral and finite-index elaboration, so this omission does not alter the translated matrix proposition.
